Brand

The AwaitIO brand

The logo, the name, the colors and the type, with files to download. The mark is a ring of pixels that fills while it waits, with the orange dot at its end: an await in progress.

Use the logo with the wordmark wherever there is room, the icon alone where there is not. Download the SVG for the web and print, the PNG where SVG is not accepted.

Clear space and minimum size

Keep free space around the logo at least as wide as the dot is tall, a quarter of the icon. The icon stays legible down to 16 px, the favicon size; below 24 px leave out the wordmark.

States

The mark doubles as the loader of the app and the favicon: it waits with the dot, fills while a step runs and turns green with a check when the step is done. Green appears nowhere else.

The loop: waiting, running, done
Waiting
Running
Done

Icons

Every icon is drawn in the same square pixels as the mark and the sun. Large icons of cards and sections use the 32 × 32 grid with the gap showing, mid-sized icons of lists and buttons the 24 × 24 grid, small icons next to text the 16 × 16 grid.

Name

AwaitIO is one word with a capital A, I and O, everywhere people read it: in text, in the UI, in titles and in slides.

Description

The short description for bios and profiles. Use it as it is, in full, so AwaitIO is described the same way everywhere.

Internal tools. Just code. Write a TypeScript function, get an admin screen for your team. No drag-and-drop. Free for up to 3 users.

132 characters, fits the 160 of an X bio

Colors

Ink on warm sand, with the sun orange as the only accent and green only for a finished step. Click a value to copy it.

Ink

Text, the ring of the logo, code windows, dark backgrounds and primary buttons.

Sun

The dot in the logo and the one accent: the sun, highlights, button shadows.

Sand

The page behind everything.

Surface

Cards and windows on the sand.

Band

The strip under the hero horizon.

Done

Only a finished step: the green ring and check.

Clay

Body text next to headings.

Line

Borders and dividers inside cards.

Typography

IBM Plex Mono for the wordmark only, Silkscreen pixels for section headings, Geist Sans for everything people read and Geist Mono for code and small labels.
